key_insight: Matryoshka Gaussian Splatting (MGS) trains a single 3D Gaussian Splatting model with nested (Matryoshka-style) components that enable smooth, continuous level-of-detail (LoD) scaling while preserving full-capacity quality.
problem_solved: Existing LoD methods for 3D Gaussian Splatting either offer only a few discrete operating points or enable continuous scaling at the cost of noticeable quality loss at full capacity; MGS makes LoD a flexible, low-cost design choice.
method: Organize Gaussians into nested subsets (a Matryoshka structure) so smaller subsets provide lower-fidelity renders and larger subsets progressively recover full detail.
Train jointly with strategies (e.g., importance-aware sampling and capacity-preserving objectives) that maintain high-quality output at full model capacity while keeping smaller subsets useful.
Provide an efficient inference selection mechanism to pick the appropriate subset given compute, memory, or bandwidth constraints for real-time LoD adjustment.
impact: MGS lets practitioners deploy a single 3DGS model that gracefully trades quality for compute/bandwidth, simplifying pipelines for streaming, real-time rendering, and resource-constrained devices while avoiding retraining multiple models.
visual_elements: Matryoshka (nested dolls) illustration mapping to nested Gaussian subsets to convey the core representation idea.
Quality vs compute plot comparing: discrete LoD steps, prior continuous LoD (quality drop at full capacity), and MGS (smooth scaling with preserved peak quality).
Side-by-side render grid showing the same scene at multiple LoD points for MGS and baseline methods to highlight fidelity retention.
Simplified training/inference pipeline diagram showing joint training, subset selection, and runtime budget-aware rendering.
paper_authors: Zhilin Guo, Boqiao Zhang, Hakan Aktas, Kyle Fogarty, Jeffrey Hu
